sketches.mechanism: The `object` keyword creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, enforced by the compiler.
sketches.resonance: Loneliness is not a feeling but a structural constraint: the language guarantees there will never be another.

sketches.mechanism: A recursive type definition where `Memory` contains a `Maybe Memory` — each memory holds the possibility of another memory inside it, or Nothing.
sketches.resonance: Every memory holds the fading possibility of another memory within it, until eventually one holds Nothing at all.
sketches.draft:
data Memory = Memory (Maybe Memory)

fade :: Memory -> Memory
fade (Memory Nothing)  = Memory Nothing
fade (Memory (Just m)) = Memory (Just (fade m))

childhood :: Memory
childhood = Memory (Just (Memory (Just (Memory Nothing))))

sketches.mechanism: Ruby's `method_missing` is called when an object receives a message it has no handler for — it can respond to anything, but has nothing real to offer.
sketches.resonance: The people-pleaser answers every call, but behind each response is the same emptiness — no real method exists.
sketches.draft:
class PeoplePleaser
  def method_missing(whatever, *)
    self
  end

  def respond_to_missing?(*, *)
    true
  end
end
